PullRequest.Title: agent host: fix: refresh local plugin copies on nested file changes
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #347835

## Why

Local agent plugins configured through `chat.pluginLocations` kept running from stale cached copies in `AgentPluginManager` after adding, editing, or deleting files in subdirectories. Three faults combined to cause this.

1. `toPluginRef` in `agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts` computed `ref.nonce` solely from `fileService.stat(plugin.uri).mtime`, which ignores nested file changes.
2. `AbstractAgentPluginDiscovery` in `agentPluginServiceImpl.ts` watched component folders with `recursive: false`, missing edits in deeper paths such as `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, newly created nested directories such as `com.github.copilot/agents/`, and plugin extensions.
3. `AgentHostAutomationCustomizations.capture` and `AgentCustomizationItemProvider._expandPluginContents` treated `undefined === undefined` nonces as cache hits.

## What changed

- Added `computePluginNonce` in `agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts` to hash sorted relative paths and metadata across the plugin tree (bounded BFS to 2,000 entries, concurrency 16, deterministic child ordering, `.git` and `node_modules` excluded, symlink cycle tracking, SHA-1 hex digest matching `AgentPluginManager._sanitize`).
- Added `getOverflowPluginNonce` backed by `IAgentPlugin.contentVersion` so trees over 2,000 entries stay stable across unrelated refreshes, advance on watched edits, and rotate on restart instead of emitting `undefined`.
- Replaced per-component non-recursive watchers inside the plugin root in `AbstractAgentPluginDiscovery` with one recursive watcher (skipping opened workspace folders so `WorkspaceWatcher` excludes are not intersected, keeping non-recursive watchers for external file components) and subscribed `AgentHostClientCustomizationsService` to `plugin.contentVersion`.
- Required defined matching nonces to reuse prior copies or cached draft expansions in `AgentHostAutomationCustomizations.capture` and `AgentCustomizationItemProvider._expandPluginContents`, while preserving clientless metadata-only automation edits.

## Verification

- `pnpm run oxlint` on all 10 changed files passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check` passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot` across `resolveCustomizationRefs.test.ts`, `agentHostClientTools.test.ts`, `agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts`, `agentPluginFormatDetection.test.ts`, `configuredAgentPluginDiscovery.test.ts`, `marketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery.test.ts`, `copilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery.test.ts`, `agentHostAutomationCustomizations.test.ts`, and `agentPluginManager.test.ts` passed (`333 passing`).
- Verified in a live Code OSS Agents window with a local plugin in `chat.pluginLocations`. Adding `com.github.copilot/agents/beta.agent.md` and `skills/second-skill/SKILL.md` (with unchanged root `mtime`), editing `skills/second-skill/SKILL.md`, and deleting `beta.agent.md` each synced a new cache revision and updated the Agents tab without restart, while writing `.git/index` triggered no resync.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The scope map is keyed by session type and normalized roots, not plugin URI; every scope subscribes to the same customization-change event. The traversal has no nonce-result or in-flight cache, and FileService forwards stat/readdir to the filesystem provider. Desktop provider calls cross main-process IPC; remote providers use the remote channel. Exact latency and typical plugin sizes are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem metadata/readdir operations and their main-process or remote IPC calls.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a non-symlink tree with F files and D non-root directories below the 2,000-entry limit, each scan performs F+D+1 provider stat calls and D+1 readdir calls. Work multiplies by the number of distinct live harness/root scopes and issued refreshes, not by sessions sharing a scope. The 16-entry limit is per scan, not global; simultaneous scopes and overlapping updates run independent batches. Warm host-copy caches do not avoid this work, and oversized-tree fallback tokens are consulted only after another scan reaches overflow.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased filesystem/IPC traffic and customization-resolution latency, with initial active-client claiming blocked on redundant scans.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same scope initialization or refresh obtained one root mtime stat per forwarded plugin. Identical scopes were already shared and refreshes already debounced, but an unchanged plugin did not incur a full-tree metadata traversal on each resolution.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every scope initialization and debounced customization refresh now walks every forwarded plugin tree, including unchanged plugins, before it can publish refs. Identical plugin instances are scanned separately across working-directory/harness scopes and across overlapping refreshes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts:338 replaces the single root fileService.stat(plugin.uri) with computePluginNonce on every toPluginRef call. The added traversal at lines 256-288 resolves every directory and stats every file, without memoizing or joining scans. resolveCustomizationRefs still maps all forwarded plugins for each scope resolution.
Findings.Title: Cache and coalesce unchanged plugin fingerprints
Findings.Impact: With a sizeable local plugin installed, starting a chat in a new working-directory scope re-scans the plugin even if an ambient scope already resolved it. Editing an unrelated prompt, changing MCP definitions, or toggling sync enablement also re-scans all unchanged plugins in every live scope. This adds potentially thousands of filesystem/IPC operations and delays initial active-client readiness; slower or remote filesystems amplify the delay and overlapping refreshes waste further I/O.
Findings.Evidence: AgentCustomizationScope.updateCustomizations (agentHostActiveClientService.ts:148-180) awaits resolveCustomizationRefs before completing initial resolution; each scope subscribes to global source changes at 189-190. acquireScope (287-309) shares only identical session-type/root scopes, while agentHostChatContribution.ts:412 creates an additional ambient scope for each harness. FileService.doResolveFile/toFileStat (fileService.ts:209-277) performs a provider stat plus readdir per directory; FileService.stat (315-320) performs another provider stat per file. diskFileSystemProviderClient.ts:81-90 forwards each operation through channel.call. ActiveClientEntry.claim (agentHostSessionHandler.ts:1304) waits for scope.whenResolved. The 50 ms Delayer only coalesces work before execution; async.ts:450-455 clears its pending promise before running the task, so a later refresh can start another scan while the earlier scan is still running.
Findings.Recommendation: Memoize and coalesce the computed nonce for watched plugins using the plugin instance and contentVersion already introduced by this PR. Invalidate on a version change or plugin replacement, avoid caching a scan against a version that changed while it ran, and retain a fresh-scan fallback for plugins without a reliable contentVersion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial agent-host customization resolution and starting a chat in a new harness/working-directory scope
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentCustomizationScope first collects files/MCP metadata, then awaits both resolveCustomizationRefs and resolveLocalCustomAgents before marking itself resolved. ActiveClientEntry.claim awaits scope.whenResolved before publishing the active-client state. Ambient scopes are initialized during harness registration even before a chat needs their plugin refs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read directory metadata and entries, stat every non-ignored file, and resolve directory symlinks as needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For an ordinary tree below the entry budget, F+D+1 provider stats and D+1 readdirs per plugin per distinct scope resolution. Symlinks can add realpath/stat work; child metadata is not eagerly requested by resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One root provider stat per forwarded plugin per scope resolution; no tree traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All plugin fingerprints must finish before scope initial resolution and active-client claiming can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward each filesystem metadata/listing request to the desktop main-process filesystem channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per provider stat/readdir/realpath, not one batched request per plugin tree. Thus ordinary scans issue F+2D+2 IPC requests per plugin per scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same desktop scope path issued one root-stat IPC request per plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Request latency contributes to every awaited scan batch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For plugins on vscode-remote resources, forward filesystem requests over the remote connection's filesystem channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same per-provider-operation cardinality as desktop IPC; scope sharing does not combine calls across different roots/harnesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One root-stat remote-channel request per forwarded plugin on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote round trips can make each sequential batch materially slower; no latency measurements were available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List source prompt files, read selected agents, read/hash forwarded source files, and write changed synthetic bundles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Files are deduplicated by URI during collection. Agent reads scale with selectable agents; bundle reads scale with effective forwarded file entries. Up to two bundle results serve an entire scope, rather than one plugin per loose file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same collection, agent reads, and bundling were already required. This PR adds tree scans alongside them, not a new MCP subprocess or server start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Collection precedes plugin fingerprinting; agent reads and bundling run alongside it and must also finish for initial resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish SessionActiveClientSet containing resolved customization refs to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One composed action per changed client view after equality checks and publication debounce, not one action per plugin entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same publication and equality suppression, but refs were ready after root metadata reads instead of complete plugin scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication waits for scope resolution; actual host-side copying is downstream of dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P forwarded plugins, including disabled forwarded plugins; F files and D non-root directories per plugin after excluding .git/node_modules and deduplicating traversed symlink targets; S distinct live session-type/root scopes rather than total sessions. Each ordinary non-overflow scan issues F+D+1 stat calls and D+1 readdir calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Identical normalized-root/session-type scopes share one AgentCustomizationScope. Different roots or harnesses do not share resolution work. Forwarded plugins run concurrently via Promise.all; each nonce traversal processes sequential batches of up to 16 entries. There is no shared fingerprint limiter or in-flight joining across scopes. Source-file bundles are serialized per authority and use a 10-operation limiter per bundler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new fingerprint traversal has no result/in-flight cache: a previously resolved ambient scope does not warm a subsequently created workspace scope. Overflow WeakMap entries retain revision tokens, not scan results. Bundle nonces reuse virtual output only after source contents have been read and hashed. Host plugin revision caching prevents repeated copies for matching nonces, but happens downstream of fingerprinting.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed traversal, lack of sharing, provider boundaries, and initial-readiness await are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical plugin tree sizes, simultaneous scope counts, and filesystem/channel latencies are unmeasured. Large asset-bearing plugins and remote filesystem plugins are realistic inputs; severity is medium rather than based on invented timing estimates.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported redundant unchanged-plugin fingerprinting. Caching/coalescing by the newly supplied plugin contentVersion can preserve freshness while removing repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live nested plugin edits, unrelated customization changes, and watcher setup/replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A relevant recursive watcher event bumps plugin.contentVersion, notifies the client customization service, and triggers component rereads where the changed path intersects a component directory. Each scope schedules a complete resolution. Changed refs are published after their scans finish; unrelated unchanged refs are equality-suppressed only after the scans.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register recursive filesystem watches; stat external paths once to select directory versus file watching; recheck missing external paths after events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One plugin-root recursive watch plus watches for external component paths. No duplicate root watch when it is exactly an opened workspace folder. External path stats occur per attached external path/recheck, not per child file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Separate correlated non-recursive watches for the root, internal component paths, and a separate manifest path. External paths previously used non-recursive watchers without the new kind stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watches enable later refreshes; async external path-kind resolution is not awaited by plugin construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and parse affected component directories/files, and reread manifests when relevant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reads scale with the component group affected by an event, not every filesystem entry under the plugin. Nested events newly reach this path; already-supported immediate-child events retain the existing readers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same component readers, but non-recursive watchers missed deeper edits. The new nested-event placement is required for the freshness behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Component results generate additional observable refreshes and update selectable customization metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rescan every forwarded plugin through filesystem-provider calls after global source notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F+2D+2 stat/listing channel calls per ordinary plugin scan, multiplied by distinct scopes and issued refreshes. The 16-entry cap is local to each scan; overlapping refreshes and scopes are not globally limited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Global source refreshes already existed, but cost one root stat per plugin. contentVersion adds notifications for arbitrary nested assets, and the new full traversal amplifies their cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads delay new refs; stale scan results are ignored only after all their operations complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize changed plugin revisions in host storage and persist the LRU; transfer source files through client filesystem resources when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical copy per missing URI/nonce revision. Cross-provider copies traverse source directories and transfer their file bytes; matching revisions do an existence check and cache persistence instead. Sync is serialized per plugin URI and concurrent across different URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same copy/cache mechanism existed. Nested changes previously reused stale nonces; issuing a fresh copy for those edits is the required functional change, not a separate performance finding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Downstream plugin synchronization/loading waits for the copy; it does not eliminate the prior client-side scan cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Relevant event batches, P forwarded plugins across S distinct live scopes, and component directories/files affected by each event. Rapid changes separated by more than the debounce can overlap full scans. Ignored .git/node_modules events are rejected before contentVersion changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One recursive root watch per watched plugin unless the root exactly matches an opened workspace folder. Inside component directories use listeners on that root watch; external directories have their own watches and external files use correlated non-recursive watchers. Discovery component reads are Promise-based without a shared global limiter. Scope Delayer debounces for 50 ms before issuance, but does not serialize running updates; sequence checks discard stale results only after work finishes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A change to one plugin or an unrelated prompt/MCP source schedules scans of all forwarded plugins. No fingerprint cache uses the versions of unchanged plugins. Matching host nonces avoid copying unchanged plugins, and matching bundle content hashes avoid rewriting virtual bundles, but neither avoids upstream reads/scans.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repeated scans and overlapping scheduling; watch resource disposal is explicitly owned by stores/MutableDisposable and is not a proven leak.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event rates and copy sizes vary. No measured burst durations; overlap follows directly from Delayer lifecycle and the absence of scan cancellation/joining.
Scenarios.Verdict: The reported fingerprint issue also covers repeated refreshes and overlap. Recursive visibility and fresh copies on actual edits are intentional; no separate watcher-lifecycle or freshness-only finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Oversized plugin trees exceeding the 2,000-entry fingerprint budget, including restart and unchanged refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: computePluginNonce starts resolving/listing the tree and only switches to getOverflowPluginNonce after enqueueChildren detects overflow. A defined fallback nonce then permits normal ref publication and downstream copy caching.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/list directories and stat the prefix of discovered plugin entries before overflow is known.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the budgeted scanned entry prefix plus root operations and current batches; listings themselves return complete immediate children. Root-wide overflow does one root stat/readdir and no child stat. Repeated refreshes repeat the same prefix/listing work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One root stat, with no prefix traversal or directory listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fallback publication still waits for the overflow scan on every resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy the whole plugin tree on a missing fallback revision and reuse existing revisions on matches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One copy per missing fallback nonce; the copy is not limited to 2,000 fingerprint entries. Stable fallback tokens prevent a copy per unrelated refresh, whereas restart intentionally creates a new revision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Root-mtime nonce reused host copies across restart; the new fallback rotation is a deliberate freshness tradeoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Downstream loading waits for materialization when the nonce is absent from host storage.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The scanned prefix up to overflow, width of each resolved directory, distinct plugin instances/contentVersion values, and S distinct scopes. A root with more than 2,000 children exits before child stats but still performs a root resolve/listing and sorts that listing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The same 16-entry batches and independent per-scope scans apply until overflow. Queue and hashed parts are entry-budgeted, but a directory listing and its child sorting happen before detecting that directory's overflow. Watcher revisions are computed synchronously after the scan returns undefined.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WeakMap tokens are stable for an unchanged plugin instance/version, advance on watched edits, and rotate on replacement/restart. They do not cache the fact of overflow or prevent subsequent prefix scans. Host revision copies can be reused for stable fallback tokens; restart rotation intentionally makes them miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repeating the overflow prefix scan despite warm fallback tokens. No independent high-confidence catastrophic memory issue was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tree shapes determine how much of the budget is read before overflow. Wide-list allocation/sorting costs and full-copy sizes were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported lack of fingerprint caching/coalescing. Fallback token generation itself avoids unversioned repeated copies; restart rotation is not reported as a separate bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization-management tabs expanding unpublished draft plugins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideChatSessionCustomizations awaits expansions before returning items. Only drafts lacking published children scan plugin directories; published children are transformed directly. Management item sources await one raw-items promise shared across tab filtering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve canonical agents/skills/commands/rules folders and read eligible Markdown metadata; synthetic agent namespaces can add directory resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four folder resolves per uncached draft plugin, plus bundle namespace resolves and metadata reads for eligible skill/agent/instruction files. One item-source promise serves all tab filters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same expansion operation, but undefined-equals-undefined incorrectly allowed reuse after source refreshes. Defined-version caching is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Item delivery waits for the expansion; versioned expansion cache hits perform none of these reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unpublished draft plugins and eligible agents, skills, instructions, and command entries. Work is per raw item-source refresh, not per tab/row; published plugins do not expand through the changed cache check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin expansions are issued concurrently, each resolves four canonical folders concurrently and reads eligible metadata files with Promise.all. ItemProviderItemSource/PureItemProviderItemSource coalesce calls through cachedPromise until a provider event invalidates it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Defined matching nonce and label continue reusing expansion children. Undefined nonces now force re-expansion when the outer item-source promise is invalidated or a provider is called directly. Normal local-plugin refs now produce defined tree/fallback nonces; undefined nonces mainly cover inaccessible/unversionable resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for limited draft-only reachability and outer request coalescing. Insufficient evidence for an independent actionable regression preserving unversioned freshness.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of genuinely unversioned drafts is unknown; no evidence shows the changed check repeatedly expanding ordinary versioned plugins per row or tab.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Rejecting unproven cache hits is required behavior, normal refs are versioned, and outer item-source caching prevents the naive per-tab fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating/updating automation customization captures and reclaiming obsolete copies
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Automation updates with a session change await capture before persisting/publishing the updated catalog. Capture iterates plugin refs, obtains/reuses a copy, and parses it. Catalog mutations and their garbage collection are sequenced; copying and parsing are on the update path, whereas an already captured automation run uses captured paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For non-local captures, copy the client plugin to staging and move it into host storage; local file clients skip copying.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero copies on prior versioned match or local in-place capture; otherwise one tree copy per ref, with per-directory listing/mkdir and per-file byte transfer across providers. An unversioned client update now creates a fresh capture rather than reusing an unproven prior copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same copy path existed on misses, but matching undefined nonces incorrectly skipped it. This PR changes that cache-hit condition to restore freshness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Automation catalog update waits for copy and staging move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source plugin bytes through the dispatching client's filesystem provider when capturing from a remote client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Source tree metadata/bytes are transferred only on a non-local copy miss, not for every versioned update or automation run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cross-client transfer on copy misses; client-originated unversioned updates now correctly cause a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote transfer is awaited before the updated capture becomes authoritative.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse manifests and component files for a newly obtained capture; list/delete obsolete unreferenced capture directories after catalog mutations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse per newly obtained/in-place recaptured plugin; cleanup lists the capture root and deletes unused directories. No new MCP subprocess is started by parsing command/launch metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same parsing and cleanup mechanisms. The changed reuse check adds parsing only when the old unversioned cache hit could not establish freshness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing is awaited by capture. Garbage collection is awaited after mutation but does not precede the successful catalog update's persistence/publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Customization refs in the updated automation, total source tree entries/bytes for remote captures, and component metadata parsed. Only session-configuration updates invoke recapture; title/trigger-only updates do not inherently rescan captured plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Capture processes plugin refs serially; parsePlugin processes component families concurrently. Cross-provider folder copy uses concurrent child operations. Automation mutation queue serializes catalog changes; cleanup is awaited in a finally block after the mutation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Defined matching nonces reuse prior captures. Without a client, metadata-only unversioned edits still reuse existing copies. Client-originated unversioned updates intentionally recapture; remote captures get unique destinations, local file clients use in-place paths. Obsolete unreferenced copies are garbage-collected; copies used by live runs remain protected by pre-existing ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for before/after reuse rules, local-copy bypass, and existing cleanup ownership; no new unbounded resource retention established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote plugin sizes and frequency of unversioned automation updates are not measured. Repeated copies are possible but are required for client updates that supply no usable version.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent finding. Defined nonce reuse and clientless metadata-only reuse are preserved; unversioned recapture is a deliberate freshness correction, not a proven avoidable performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all ten changed files and all diff pages against base 384f593b5a4c1315b1168e4d4b32e9168752f6a0. Submitted one medium-severity, high-confidence finding for repeated uncached plugin-tree fingerprint scans across distinct scopes and source refreshes. Checked traversal budget, provider IPC/remote boundaries, scheduling overlap, watcher disposal, draft expansion coalescing, host-copy caching, automation capture/cleanup, and transitive parsing/bundling. No concrete performance-regression fix with qualifying provenance was established; freshness fixes were not misclassified as performance-fix signals. Static read-only review; performance magnitude was not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
